text:
Arber Xhekaj has four points in 20 games. That's the same total he managed in 65 games last season, and it's why Sportsnaut is calling this his best season in Montreal. The 25-year-old, who signed as an undrafted free agent in 2021, plays about 12 minutes a night, has 41 hits, and still owns one of the league's heaviest shots: his hardest this season was clocked at 99.45 mph, 99th percentile.

Our numbers like the defensive side more than the scoring. At five on five Montreal has taken 53% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) with him on, 3.2 points better than when he sits. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him stopping 15% of the entries aimed at him last season, against a typical 11%.

The points are the part to doubt. His scoring rate sits above the top of our talent range for him, and over his last ten games we'd have expected about 1.5 points, not four. Evolving-Hockey had his team creating almost nothing with him on last season. He doesn't need points to keep his spot; the question is whether the rest holds as Montreal comes off two straight losses.
